items.title: Milt Fillius interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 18, 2000
items.q: but it was Joe Williams and Milt Hinton were sitting down at the Alexander Hamilton Inn across the table. Joe was on one side and I was on the other and they started talking.

ctx.x: Well you have a beautiful building named after you and I think the most lasting thing of course is going to be this jazz archive. And I’d love to just actually hear again how this idea came to your head.

Well it started with the Gibson parties in Colorado Springs and later in Denver, when I realized that every year some people did not appear again, they were gone. And they used to pay tribute to them. And I though jeez, there they’ve gone, and there’s nothing. There’s really nothing left behind. And then — I forget when it was — but it was Joe Williams and Milt Hinton were sitting down at the Alexander Hamilton Inn across the table. Joe was on one side and I was on the other and they started talking. And they…
and he said I have an idea I want to do Milt’s life, and all his old friends and so on. And he said I’m going to apply to the National —
